cues.text: Many years ago, I journeyed with the Maharajah of India
to the island of Time, intending to claim its secrets.
What we discovered was a barren, ruined place,
its halls deserted, and its guardians gone to sand.
Strange tales adorned its walls, which spoke of an empress, an empress of time.

The books showed me that life eternal was not beyond my reach,

But you were gone. They were gone. Or so I thought.
I turned my attention towards other pursuits and left that dream behind.
But then, four weeks ago, the dagger stirred and showed me things,
whispered to me in my sleep. It drew me here towards Babylon.
Alas, the Maharajah did not share my vision, would not grant me leave.
So I slew him and claimed his kingdom, his army for my own.
Nothing would stand between me and my desire.
I am Zurvan, God of time, and I bear gifts, pain, and suffering.
Come closer, that I might share these treasures with you.
I came offering power, and this is how you respond.

cues.text: The prince cleansed himself in the waters of the fountain.
Though returned to a normal body, the same could not be said for his mind.
The prince was finally forced to accept the fact that Farah
was lost to him, and that he alone was responsible for this.
Had he not hidden the truth from her, had he shown more compassion,
then perhaps things may have gone another way. But now it was simply too late.
In spite of this, or perhaps because of it, the prince found himself profoundly
affected by Farah's earlier words and deeds. They had wrought a change in him,
slowly supplanting the dark demands of his ruthless alter ego.

cues.text: The prince's spirits were lifted by the release of the trapped citizens.
He rode now for the palace, not to reclaim his birthright,
but to save his kingdom and its people.
And so the prince's eyes had finally been opened to the true nature of his
corrupt half, that cruel and charismatic voice which once whispered in his ear.
It had subtly encouraged our burdened hero to do wrong.
But now the voice was stilled, the prince's mind once more his own.
You may wonder why I would let this come to pass.
So many dead and likely more to follow. An empire reduced to rubble.
A prince cast to the streets and hunted like a common criminal.
But I had seen the timeline. And of all the outcomes lay bare to me,
this one held the most promise of them all.
For the prince would have an opportunity to set things right.
Watch now. See the thing of which I speak.
The prince made his way along the torn and blasted district,
haunted by visions from his past.
The darkside tavern where he'd spent many late nights was now reduced to cinders.
Babylon's proud armada, which he would often come to greet,
lay cracked and broken, cast to the bottom of the Euphrates.
You should know that it was not love that drove him, but duty. I was his
responsibility. He had made a promise, a promise that was now broken and undone.
As with all mistakes he had made, the prince meant to fix this.
A noble goal, to be certain, but a selfish one as well.
For he was motivated to ease his own pain.

cues.text: When the prince was struck by the sands of time, something was woken within.
Something strange and cunning, something dark.
The seven years spent on the run had embittered the prince and made him hard.
This burden sustained his other half, gave it strength.
The prince was tempted to do as it said, for it was a light in the darkness,
offering comfort and guidance to a man who had just lost everything.
But what were its intentions? Why did it help him? Only time would tell.

cues.text: And so once more the prince began the journey home,
his mind afire with visions of the justice he would visit upon the vizier.
While somewhat demanding, his invisible companion proved a valuable ally,
helping to avoid the many enemies and obstacles encountered along the way.
The prince fled from the arena, embarrassed by the unwanted attention,
fearful that they might realize he was becoming a sand monster.
But something tugged at him. The freed citizens believed he had come to rescue them.
That people, his people, now lived when they should have died.
This was just an accident.
His thoughts had been only of reaching the vizier and exacting revenge.
Perhaps now the prince would remember he once fought for something
other than his lost honor. It was simply too soon to tell.
With the Dahaka defeated, the prince was slowly regaining pieces of his former self.
The pressure and desperation which once drove him were gone.
Grim as things seemed, there was now hope.
Hope that peace could be restored to the land and to our tortured hero.
But the vizier's armies still hunted him. And they grew more determined by the hour.
And so the prince and Farah separated. She sought to save lives, he to end them.
For the prince intended to confront his enemy and perhaps utilize
the powerful warriors who had holed up inside the temple.
His mind churned with thoughts of glorious vengeance. But something new as well.
Descending into the depths, his thoughts kept returning to Farah.
He wondered if she was thinking of him as well.
Babylon had finally fallen and none were left to come to the prince's aid.
He was now the city's only hope. If he failed, his entire world could be lost.
For the vizier was not content to simply be a king. No. He fancied himself a god.
The question now was whether the prince realized the position he was in.
And if he did, would he accept this responsibility? Would he become a hero?
So she had reached the prince. He feared for her safety. Even if it was
just one person, at least now he thought of someone other than himself.
Poor prince. His secret self had been revealed,
and Farah quite disturbed by what she had seen.
Perhaps he should have been honest from the beginning.
Too late he realized his mistake in staying silent.

cues.speaker: Vizier
cues.text: Not quite the homecoming you expected.

cues.speaker: Kaileena
cues.text: As our ship lay sinking in the harbor, the prince found

cues.speaker: Kaileena
cues.text: himself in a city quite different from the one he left behind.

cues.speaker: Kaileena
cues.text: The normally busy wharves were now decimated. Blood-spattered awnings

cues.speaker: Kaileena
cues.text: and splintered door frames were all that waited to greet him.

cues.speaker: Kaileena
cues.text: And the people, merchants, beggars, fishermen, were nowhere to be found.

cues.speaker: Kaileena
cues.text: Others had taken their place.

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: Let her go.

lines.speaker: Prince
trigger: No static reference in the game data; started by engine or script code (events 880001)

cues.text: Why is it that every time disaster strikes I find myself
without a proper blade? Still, it's better than nothing.

lines.speaker: Prince
trigger: No static reference in the game data; started by engine or script code (events 880002)
lines.text: Kaileena! No!

trigger: No static reference in the game data; started by engine or script code (events 88001B)

cues.speaker: Farah
cues.text: It seems I chose the right moment to return.

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: Thank you.

cues.speaker: Dark Prince
cues.text: Lucky shot.

cues.speaker: Farah
cues.text: We should move. I'm sure more are on the way.

trigger: No static reference in the game data; started by engine or script code (events 88001D)

cues.speaker: Mahasti
cues.text: You waste your time. The Vizier has already begun to transform

cues.speaker: Mahasti
cues.text: the women I have imprisoned. You buy yourself hours at most.

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: If I had some sands for every time someone said that to me.
Oh! I do.

cues.speaker: Farah
cues.text: The women are free and headed to safety. It was right of you to return. Prince?
You...

cues.speaker: Farah
cues.text: You're one of them?

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: No, Farah! This is not how it appears!

cues.speaker: Farah
cues.text: You're a sand monster! You lied to me all this time!

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: No, I have been tainted by the sands. This is true,

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: but my mind and my heart are my own. Please believe me.

cues.speaker: Farah
cues.text: Stay away from me.

trigger: No static reference in the game data; started by engine or script code (events 88001E)

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: Do you see now? The change was physical, nothing more!

cues.speaker: Farah
cues.text: Why should I believe you? Everything you have done contradicts this.

cues.speaker: Farah
cues.text: I have seen the way you hunger for combat. You take pleasure in creating death.

cues.speaker: Farah
cues.text: Your constant talk of bloody vengeance, your cold disregard for your own people.

cues.speaker: Farah
cues.text: You heard the women in the brothel as clearly as I did, yet you turned away.

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: But I came back. I came back for you.

cues.speaker: Farah
cues.text: You are a prince in title only.

cues.speaker: Farah
cues.text: Go and reclaim your throne.

cues.speaker: Farah
cues.text: But know this. You do so alone.

cues.speaker: Dark Prince
cues.text: You certainly have a way with women.

cues.speaker: Dark Prince
cues.text: Those you don't get killed can't get far enough away from you.

trigger: No static reference in the game data; started by engine or script code (events 880020)

cues.text: Poor prince!

cues.speaker: Vizier
cues.text: Locked inside a burning building and no way out! Too bad for you!

cues.speaker: Dark Prince
cues.text: Well, look at that.
A trap.

cues.speaker: Dark Prince
cues.text: Do you see now what happens when you try to help other people?
You die! Enoch is in here! Going to burn! Almost, please! Helmut!
Over here! Over here! Please! Find the way we have enough!

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: Father, give me guidance. Lend me strength.
Where have you gone?

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: Father. Gone.
Wait, that's it!

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: Where is the machinery that controls these conveyors?
Quickly, please!

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: There is not much time!
Above us! The stairs are burned, though. You will never be able to reach it.

lines.speaker: Prince
trigger: No static reference in the game data; started by engine or script code (events 880022)

cues.text: Separated again. I'll be with you soon. I need to find a way to open this door.

trigger: No static reference in the game data; started by engine or script code (events 880023)

cues.speaker: Farah
cues.text: Incredible. I have only heard stories of such marvels.

cues.speaker: Farah
cues.text: But to see one up close... Is there not a similar device in Azad?

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: This lift will bring us to the throne room. But wonder of wonders,

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: it seems to have stopped working. I will try and return it to life.

cues.speaker: Farah
cues.text: I do hope to visit Azad someday.

trigger: No static reference in the game data; started by engine or script code (events 880025)

cues.speaker: Farah
cues.text: What is he like? Your father?

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: He is a good man.
No.

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: A great man. Strong, loyal, kind, forgiving.

cues.speaker: Farah
cues.text: What is it?
I.

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: That is to say. We did not part on the best of terms.

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: It was many years ago. I was young and full of pride, full of fear as well.

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: He offered to listen, but I could not find the words, would not find them.

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: And I only hope that I may see him once more. To say that I am sorry.

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: But this is a story for another time. Let us speak of other things.

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: Surrounded by so much sadness, we should not succumb ourselves.

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: Returning to the matter at hand, I cannot get to you from where I am.

cues.speaker: Farah
cues.text: I can close another shutter then. Let us regroup ahead.

trigger: No static reference in the game data; started by engine or script code (events 880026)

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: There is still no way for me to get to you.

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: However, you can reach the throne room from where you stand,

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: and I can pass through the greenhouse.

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: This will certainly bring us to the same location.

cues.speaker: Farah
cues.text: Be careful, Prince.

trigger: No static reference in the game data; started by engine or script code (events 880027)

cues.speaker: Vizier
cues.text: Do not take another step. I am impressed you made it past my little welcoming party.

cues.speaker: Vizier
cues.text: Impressed, but also quite annoyed. You have robbed me of my strongest allies.

cues.speaker: Vizier
cues.text: It would be unfair of me not to return the favor.

cues.speaker: Vizier
cues.text: Farah will make an excellent queen, fit for a god.

cues.speaker: Vizier
cues.text: Although we will need to make some modifications.

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: Let her go!

cues.speaker: Vizier
cues.text: You act as though you have a say in the matter.

cues.speaker: Vizier
cues.text: Which you don't.

cues.speaker: Vizier
cues.text: Say hello to your father.

lines.speaker: Kaileena
trigger: No static reference in the game data; started by engine or script code (events 880028)

cues.text: The prince was cast to his death into a pit of darkness, robbed of Farah,
distanced from the vizier. He had been warned that his journey would not end well.
Ah, but do not be surprised. The prince's transformation saved him.
Sometimes good can come of ill. Sometimes.

trigger: No static reference in the game data; started by engine or script code (events 880029)

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: Father's sword? But what is it doing here?
Oh, come on now!

cues.speaker: Dark Prince
cues.text: Did you really expect to find him alive?

cues.speaker: Dark Prince
cues.text: Even after everything you have experienced, still you hold out hope.

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: Oh, father. What have I done?

cues.speaker: Dark Prince
cues.text: What now, then? Gather up enough sand, perform another grand rewind?

cues.speaker: Dark Prince
cues.text: Or perhaps you can return to the island and travel back to a time when he

cues.speaker: Dark Prince
cues.text: might still be saved. Maybe rescue a damsel in distress along the way.

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: No! You are right. I have been like a child. Naive and arrogant,

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: always rushing to undo my mistakes, never facing the consequences of my actions.

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: No more. I accept what I have done. And all that it implies.

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: What is this?

cues.speaker: Dark Prince
cues.text: You have no water.
How did you.

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: You hold no power over me now. Be gone.

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: Retreat to whatever dark hole spawned you, and do not trouble me again.

lines.speaker: Farah
trigger: No static reference in the game data; started by engine or script code (events 88002D)

cues.text: Prince, leave this place. It reeks of sadness and cruel intentions.
You must not chase this shadow. Turn away. Wake up. I will lead you.

trigger: No static reference in the game data; started by engine or script code (events 880033)

cues.text: Let us hope! If I crash, it is the end for both of us! The prince!

cues.speaker: Vizier
cues.text: Stop him!

cues.speaker: Kaileena
cues.text: And so once more the prince began the journey home,

cues.speaker: Kaileena
cues.text: his mind afire with visions of the justice he would visit upon the vizier.

trigger: No static reference in the game data; started by engine or script code (events 880034)

cues.speaker: Kaileena
cues.text: Everything had come full circle. The prince had resurrected his greatest enemy.

cues.speaker: Kaileena
cues.text: Worse, he had accidentally delivered me into the man's hands,

cues.speaker: Kaileena
cues.text: unleashing a nightmare plague across Babylon. As if this was not enough,

cues.speaker: Kaileena
cues.text: the prince had nearly been transformed by the sands himself.

cues.speaker: Kaileena
cues.text: Though he had avoided death, he had not escaped entirely untouched.

cues.speaker: Dark Prince
cues.text: Wake up, Prince. Wake up.
Wake up.

trigger: No static reference in the game data; started by engine or script code (events 880036)

cues.text: We made it. Hold your horses.

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: Come on.

trigger: No static reference in the game data; started by engine or script code (events 880037)

cues.text: What?

cues.speaker: Farah
cues.text: What is that thing?
It's the vizier!

cues.speaker: Farah
cues.text: What's happened to him?

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: Something terrible.

cues.speaker: Dark Prince
cues.text: Something wonderful.
Wait! No!

cues.speaker: Farah
cues.text: Be happy that he is gone. You never would have stood a chance.

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: Oh, how silly of me. You're right.

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: Perhaps we should surrender. Or turn away and leave the city.

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: I know a lovely little island just a few weeks' journey from here.

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: I'm sure by the time we return, this will all be sorted out.

cues.speaker: Farah
cues.text: If it comforts you to mock me, then by all means continue. But you are so focused on

cues.speaker: Farah
cues.text: killing him, you've thrown strategy completely out the window. You could have died.

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: I suppose. But now we need to find a way to

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: enter the temple. We're wasting time here.

cues.speaker: Farah
cues.text: That seems to be our best bet.

trigger: No static reference in the game data; started by engine or script code (events 880038)

cues.speaker: Farah
cues.text: See, you did it.

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: We did it.

trigger: No static reference in the game data; started by engine or script code (events 880039)

cues.text: Wait!

cues.speaker: Farah
cues.text: There are people hurt inside! We should help them!

cues.speaker: Dark Prince
cues.text: Now is not the time, Prince. You can help all you want later.

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: Go, Farah. Tend to the wounded.

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: I will catch up with you once I've dealt with the Vizier.

trigger: No static reference in the game data; started by engine or script code (events 88003A)

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: To conquer a city is one thing, but to do so with such violence and cruelty is

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: something else entirely. I will return every blow he has landed against my kingdom.

cues.speaker: Dark Prince
cues.text: We are close, Prince. So close. Let us make him suffer.

trigger: No static reference in the game data; started by engine or script code (events 88003B)

cues.speaker: Farah
cues.text: Are you alright?

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: He has escaped. And you, what of the troops?

cues.speaker: Farah
cues.text: Dead. All dead. But I saw the vizier,

cues.speaker: Farah
cues.text: or whatever it is he's become. He flew towards the palace.

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: Then we know where to go.

trigger: No static reference in the game data; started by engine or script code (events 88003C)

cues.speaker: Farah
cues.text: Thank you, Prince.
Of course.

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: The problem is, now I am trapped.

cues.speaker: Dark Prince
cues.text: Just like a woman, solving her problem creates a new one for you.

cues.speaker: Farah
cues.text: Allow me to return the favor, then.

lines.speaker: Farah
trigger: No static reference in the game data; started by engine or script code (events 88003D)

cues.text: I can see the palace from here. Make your way to me.

trigger: No static reference in the game data; started by engine or script code (events 88003E)

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: At last we have returned.

cues.speaker: Farah
cues.text: Did you hear that?

cues.speaker: Dark Prince
cues.text: If you know what is good for you, say no.

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: Farah, we must press on. I am sure she will be alright.

cues.speaker: Farah
cues.text: Are you mad? She was begging for her life. She said there were others.

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: No, we can afford no more delays.
Good.

cues.speaker: Dark Prince
cues.text: Put her in her place.

cues.speaker: Farah
cues.text: These are your people. You are their prince. And yet you would leave them to suffer.

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: That man has taken everything from me.

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: And now that I have the opportunity to punish him, you want to delay me?

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: Have you forgotten what he did to you?

cues.speaker: Farah
cues.text: But I...

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: You are burdened by a guilty conscience, Farah.

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: He made you watch as your people suffered, unable to aid them.

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: You are not to blame. Do not let it cloud your judgment.

cues.speaker: Farah
cues.text: It is not I who suffers from clouded judgment.

cues.speaker: Farah
cues.text: You may choose not to help them, but you cannot stop me.

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: I go to kill the vizier to end this while you

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: run about applying bandages to axe wounds.

cues.speaker: Dark Prince
cues.text: Good riddance. She has been nothing but a distraction,

cues.speaker: Dark Prince
cues.text: always getting into trouble and slowing us down. Finally, we can.
What?

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: Something could happen to her.

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: I cannot lose her again.
No, no, no!

cues.speaker: Dark Prince
cues.text: We are so close!

trigger: No static reference in the game data; started by engine or script code (events 88003F)

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: Farah!

cues.speaker: Farah
cues.text: What do you want?

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: I have thought about what you said, and you are right.
I.

cues.speaker: Farah
cues.text: Can't you see we're in the middle of a conversation?

cues.speaker: Farah
cues.text: If you really do desire death, kindly wait your turn.

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: I have killed most of the guards. It should be safe.

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: Go and find the women. Free them. I will deal with her.

lines.speaker: Vizier
trigger: No static reference in the game data; started by engine or script code (events 880040)

cues.text: No, no, not now

trigger: No static reference in the game data; started by engine or script code (events 880035)

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: Babylon, but so far away. As a child, father would tell me stories.

cues.speaker: Dark Prince
cues.text: Attention! Something's happening down there.

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: It's the vizier! He has been completely transformed!
Interesting.

cues.speaker: Dark Prince
cues.text: He has used the power of the sands to transform his army.

cues.speaker: Dark Prince
cues.text: And these artifacts will allow him to transport them across the city with ease.

cues.speaker: Dark Prince
cues.text: He appears to be in complete control.

cues.speaker: Dark Prince
cues.text: Things do not look too good for you at the moment.

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: I will not let the vizier have Babylon. My city! My throne!

lines.speaker: Prince
trigger: No static reference in the game data; started by engine or script code (events 880021, 880043)

cues.text: All right, I will admit, I was not expecting that.

trigger: CGI cinematic Video/Cine/P3C_010, English audio track (Bink track 0)
lines.note: Hand-curated from Parakeet and Whisper transcripts of the mix and the isolated vocals.

cues.speaker: Kaileena
cues.text: We all make mistakes. Some are small. Some are large.

cues.speaker: Kaileena
cues.text: But his mistake, born of innocence, fueled by pride,

cues.speaker: Kaileena
cues.text: was the greatest and most terrible of them all.
All that is yours is rightfully ours. You cannot change your fate.

cues.speaker: Kaileena
cues.text: Some believed, when the prince journeyed to the Island of Time to escape death,

cues.speaker: Kaileena
cues.text: that he returned alone. The amulet destroyed, the Dahaka appeased, the Empress dead.

cues.speaker: Kaileena
cues.text: The prince was free at last. But this is not how it happened.

cues.speaker: Kaileena
cues.text: The truth is that he chose to save me from my destiny.

cues.speaker: Kaileena
cues.text: In doing so, he set me free and doomed us all.

cues.speaker: Kaileena
cues.text: Prince, of all the possible futures, this one

cues.speaker: Kaileena
cues.text: held the most promise that something has changed.

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: Do not worry, Kaileena. No harm will come to you in Babylon.

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: I promise. Look, we are nearly home.

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: Kaileena!

trigger: CGI cinematic Video/Cine/P3C_020, English audio track (Bink track 0)
lines.note: Hand-curated from Parakeet and Whisper transcripts of the mix and the isolated vocals.

cues.speaker: Kaileena
cues.text: This is how it happened. This is how I died.
No!
What have we here?

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: The Vizier!

cues.speaker: Vizier
cues.text: Ah, you must be the Prince of Persia. Come home at last. Too late, I'm afraid.

cues.speaker: Vizier
cues.text: I believe I have something of yours.

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: No! Kaileena!

cues.speaker: Vizier
cues.text: The promise of power fulfilled! I will be immortal!

trigger: CGI cinematic Video/Cine/P3C_030, English audio track (Bink track 0)
lines.note: Hand-curated from Parakeet and Whisper transcripts of the mix and the isolated vocals.

cues.text: Keep away from me!

trigger: CGI cinematic Video/Cine/P3C_040, English audio track (Bink track 0)
lines.note: Hand-curated from Parakeet and Whisper transcripts of the mix and the isolated vocals.

cues.speaker: Citizen
cues.text: My dear friends, I tell you now and true, it is the Prince of Persia!

cues.speaker: Citizen
cues.text: The Prince of Persia? That can't be. He's come back to us!

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: It is good to see you safe.

trigger: CGI cinematic Video/Cine/P3C_050, English audio track (Bink track 0)
lines.note: Hand-curated from Parakeet and Whisper transcripts of the mix and the isolated vocals.

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: Be on your guard.

cues.speaker: Farah
cues.text: I always am.
Run!

cues.speaker: Citizen
cues.text: All hail the Prince of Persia, the greatest hero the land has ever known!

cues.speaker: Citizen
cues.text: You have saved the people of this city, and we have come to repay the favor!

cues.speaker: Citizen
cues.text: You cannot kill these creatures, but we can slow them. Go, Prince!

cues.speaker: Citizen
cues.text: Find the Vizier and finish him, so that this nightmare might finally end.

trigger: CGI cinematic Video/Cine/P3C_060, English audio track (Bink track 0)
lines.note: Hand-curated from Parakeet and Whisper transcripts of the mix and the isolated vocals.

cues.speaker: Vizier
cues.text: This is not what the dagger promised!

cues.speaker: Kaileena
cues.text: This world was not meant for me. But there are others,

cues.speaker: Kaileena
cues.text: and I will find my place, just as you have found yours.

cues.speaker: Kaileena
cues.text: Be free now, Prince. Your journey is at an end.

cues.speaker: Farah
cues.text: What is it?

cues.speaker: Dark Prince
cues.text: All that is yours is rightfully mine, and mine it will be.

trigger: CGI cinematic Video/Cine/P3C_070, English audio track (Bink track 0)
lines.note: Hand-curated from Parakeet and Whisper transcripts of the mix and the isolated vocals.

cues.speaker: Farah
cues.text: Wake up. Wake up.

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: Farah?

cues.speaker: Farah
cues.text: Are you alright?

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: I think... I think it's finally over.

cues.speaker: Farah
cues.text: Prince, there's still something I don't understand. How did you really know my name?

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: Most people think time is like a river that flows swift and sure in one direction.

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: But I have seen the face of time, and I can tell you, they are wrong.

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: Time is an ocean in a storm. You may wonder who I really am, and why I say this.

cues.speaker: Prince
cues.text: Come, and I will tell you a tale like none you have ever heard.
